title: Gate 3 release authorization for a paired browser (owner-gated)
description:
Production prerequisite of task-817d893fa1254a4d82d2888af1f87a47, filed by architect-f362f7a6 after owner ruling comment-933e6a7c preserved the FULL evidence -> browser approve -> PR-link proof. Measurement in parent comment-4157b81a24544fab8ca45702d1843fd5 at b1da2cb9d88515dcfce1046d0cac0a0eaeed01de. This is NOT the missing contract-bound lane helper; that remains independently owned by task-6bafd3b9439640cba358dd6e79329c9d.

OBJECTIVE: resolve and enforce the exact browser identity allowed to spend release.decide without opening MCP, impersonating the configured operator, or changing evidence/admission/replay authority. This row is OWNER-GATED before any production authority change. Candidate for the owner's decision: a release-only authorization arm for a currently authenticated, project-bound durable HUMAN with ADMIN, retaining its own principal id; configured operator behavior remains unchanged. The candidate is NOT approved by the parent's preserve-scope ruling. The owner may instead require an explicit operator step-up design; if that requires a new command/wire, split its producer work before implementation under the epic rails.

MEASURED GAP: main.tsx:75-76/114+ uses real pairing and live-handshake.ts:170-185 carries its minted credential; http-listener-pairing-principal.test.ts:109-134 pins a HUMAN/session id distinct from the configured operator. daemon-command-registry.ts:330-336 selects the ASYNC release entry before the sync paired-human waiver. daemon-command-async-entries.ts:275-285 composes createReleaseDecideHandler. release-decide-command.ts:32-35 and release-decide-service.ts:118-120 both require exact operatorPrincipalId; the unconfigured fallback is separately fenced at async-entries.ts:186-190. OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS includes release and MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS derives from it at mcp-tool-allowlist.ts:94. Changing only the synchronous waiver does nothing; deleting the roster entry also opens MCP and is forbidden.

FRESH CONTROL: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec vitest run --root . --config package.json src/release/release-decide-wiring.test.ts -t "fences a non-operator principal even when fully composed"` EXIT 0; Test Files 1 passed (1); Tests 1 passed | 5 skipped (6), 4.71s. This production-registry arm confirms OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_REQUIRED @ DAEMON_AUTHORIZATION. It does not claim a live browser pass.

DELIVERABLE after explicit owner approval: one focused release authorization policy composed at every reachable release entry, with positive/negative tests and unchanged command identity, evidence checks, durable receipts and MCP exclusion. Expected implementation envelope is <=8 named files, with production modules <=250 lines; pin exact files when policy is approved. No new command kind is assumed.

NOT IN SCOPE: completing the contract-goal harness, editing the browser proof to use configured credentials, replacing a click with direct operator dispatch, hand-seeding evidence, changing the operator/MCP roster, live PR creation, main integration, or unrelated gate widening. No source edits before the owner's specific ruling is recorded.

EXACT focused verification command: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec vitest run --root . --config package.json src/release`. Run fresh foreground, nonzero count lines required. The owning plan also names the existing MCP exclusion test and full daemon regression. Parent task-817d893f retains full live-browser acceptance and the existing epic-final task-6cbcf5ff retains whole-epic hardening; do not create a separate evidence row.
definitionOfDone: Before production edits, an owner-authored or explicitly attributed owner ruling in a row comment selects the exact release-only authorization instrument and resolves its compatibility with the epic's operator-only rail. The plan has an explicit STOP before authority-changing steps. If not approved, remain blocked; neither scope preservation nor SPEED auto-approval supplies this authorization.

The approved policy is composed at every reachable release admission layer, including the durable command wrapper, service and unconfigured branch where applicable. Authenticated actor identity remains the actual caller; no operator impersonation, browser credential injection or parallel authorization implementation. Existing configured-operator behavior is preserved.

Production-surface tests prove the approved browser principal reaches release admission while agent, unknown/non-current session, wrong-project and insufficient-capability principals refuse with exact code AND layer before dossier, publication or PR effects; assert zero side-effect calls on refused arms and include replay/actor-identity coverage.

release.decide remains in the operator/human-only classification and excluded from MCP, with bidirectional served/excluded roster assertions. No other command's authorization changes; tests include a non-release operator kind as a negative control.

Focused `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec vitest run --root . --config package.json src/release` and the plan's MCP/daemon gates run fresh foreground with nonzero test counts and exit statuses. Record one bounded mutation proving the chosen authorization predicate is load-bearing, prove exact restoration, and disclose path-attributed foreign failures rather than calling them green.
taskRails: OWNER APPROVAL IS A HARD STOP before production authorization edits. The parent's scope ruling is not a waiver of operator-only authority and does not choose this policy.
Do not remove release.decide from OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS or alter derived MCP exclusions; do not substitute the configured operator credential/principal into browser requests.
The async release path bypasses the synchronous registry waiver. Trace and test the actual command wrapper plus service; no one-line sync waiver claimed as a fix.
Keep this a focused production authorization slice with its own tests. The parent owns end-to-end release proof and the existing epic-final owns full integration hardening.

implementationPlan.description: OWNER-AUTHORIZATION STOP / BASELINE (DoD 1). Before ANY authority-changing edit, read and cite comment-e9ecfd4c3cef4a438ba4873e5627742e: the human approved only currently authenticated, project-bound durable HUMAN + ADMIN for release.decide, with actual identity retained, configured operator preserved and MCP exclusion unchanged. If that exact ruling is missing, superseded or contradicted, STOP and report_blocked; SPEED is not a waiver. Do not revive the rejected operator-step-up alternative. Read current task context and both DONE producer completion/review summaries. Record HEAD and owned-path status; preserve all peer dirt. Capture the required repo-wide baseline at the task's merge-base using existing recorded, reproducible gate evidence if available; no branch switch, reset, stash or sibling worktree. This is an authority/preflight step, not a duplicate implementation or a full-suite run after every edit.

TEST FIRST (DoD 2-4). Build a test-tier harness using SqliteEventStore.openEphemeralForProjectTest, ensureGenesisRecoveryBinding, createDaemonCommandPorts and the REAL createSessionAuthenticator, following repository-bootstrap-authorization.test.ts. Use startControlRoomListener with the production createOperatorSessionHandshakePort; the positive browser identity must come from /session/pair/request -> listener.approvePairing -> /session/pair/claim, not a hand-written AuthenticatedPrincipal or configured operator credential. Construct a normal four-field release payload on a fresh release aggregate and send it through /command. Fully compose release's production handler with counting dossier/publisher/PR effect ports; deliberately leave the remote unbound so an authorized request reaches exact RELEASE_REMOTE_MISSING @ PROJECT_REDUCER at DISPATCH, while current code instead fails OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_REQUIRED @ DAEMON_AUTHORIZATION. Assert the paired id differs from operator, the durable command decision uses the paired id, and the operator key is absent. Add cases for HUMAN with GOAL but no ADMIN; ADMIN but no GOAL; a valid agent session with no durable HUMAN principal; unknown, exactly-expired and CLOSED credentials; cross-project credential use; direct command-boundary project mismatch; configured operator unchanged; authorized but unconfigured release; and a non-release operator command such as goal.close remaining denied to the same paired ADMIN. For session close/agent setup reuse session-test-fixtures.ts send/envelope/openPayload against runSessionCommand, with explicit fixture project/session overrides, rather than writing accepted authority rows. Bound each HTTP operation; close listener/store in finally/afterEach on success, refusal and thrown assertions. No bearer-bearing logs or snapshots. Run the narrow new spec to show the intended positive-authorization assertion RED before implementation; do not change the expected prerequisite refusal to today's operator refusal.

ADD ONE RELEASE-ONLY AUTHORIZATION ASSERTION IN THE EXISTING COMMAND MODULE (DoD 2-3). Add/export assertReleasePrincipal(input, options), with narrowly typed options carrying store, projectId and operatorPrincipalId, and reuse it from admittedInput. Keep the configured-operator branch unchanged. The ONLY new disjunct is envelope.commandKind === release.decide AND principal.projectId === options.projectId AND authenticated principal capabilities include CAPABILITIES.ADMIN AND isDurableHumanPrincipal(options.store, principal.principalId). Use existing CAPABILITIES and human-approver imports; introduce no layer/code/roster. Unknown/unreadable principal data and failed durable reads must fail closed with the existing OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_REQUIRED / DAEMON_AUTHORIZATION / 403, never an unhandled exception or successful fallback. Authentication remains the separate production ingress check, not something this helper claims to perform; document the trust contract. Keep the existing project mismatch check, payload validation, command/base identity digest, expected-version admission, pending-command exclusion and actual-principal decision keys unchanged. Do not rewrite the principal, session credential, request bytes or replay identity. Keep this production file <=250 lines; its existing .js bridge already reexports the new internal symbol.

COMPOSE THE SAME ASSERTION AT THE OTHER RELEASE ENTRY POINTS (DoD 2). Replace the inner service's exact-operator-only guard with assertReleasePrincipal, passing existing options; do not duplicate the disjunct or change release evidence, publisher, receipt or PR logic. Pass the needed existing store/project/operator options into unconfiguredReleaseHandler and use that SAME assertion there before its unchanged RELEASE_PR_FAILED refusal. Authorized paired ADMIN must reach the honest missing-composition refusal; unauthorized callers must still stop at authorization first. Keep the release entry's kind, capability GOAL, payloadKeys and all other async command entries unchanged. Do not touch the synchronous registry waiver or OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS/MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS. Remove an import only if this change makes it unused; no unrelated refactor. The service must stay <=250 lines and async-entries must stay below 400 (currently 378); the small guard replacement should shrink or keep them bounded.

COMPLETE DISCRIMINATING AUTHORITY/REPLAY ARMS (DoD 3-4). Ensure each refused case asserts its OWN enforcement boundary: no ADMIN despite GOAL -> OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_REQUIRED + DAEMON_AUTHORIZATION + 403; missing GOAL -> CAPABILITY_DENIED + AUTHORIZE + 403; unknown/CLOSED/at-expiry/cross-project credential -> AUTHENTICATION_FAILED + AUTHENTICATE + 401. Direct command-boundary wrong-project and non-HUMAN inputs must not acquire the new disjunct; preserve configured-operator wrong-project RELEASE_PROJECT_MISMATCH. Assert zero dossier/publish/PR calls and no new release admission/receipt for authorization refusals. Exercise unconfigured paired ADMIN -> RELEASE_PR_FAILED @ RUNNER_WORKSPACE and the matching unconfigured non-ADMIN authorization refusal. Replay the authorized prerequisite refusal with the SAME still-current credential and command, proving its durable key remains the real paired id; after expiry/closure the SAME replay must fail at AUTHENTICATE rather than reuse a cached decision. A second independently minted HUMAN cannot replay the first actor's record; assert the existing version/command refusal rather than accepting the first decision. Include throw/unreadable durable principal lookup coverage through the production assertion without changing global identity behavior. For the non-release negative control use the same principal with required GOAL so an earlier capability refusal cannot mask the operator fence. Rely on the existing bidirectional mcp-tool-allowlist.test.ts for served/excluded set equality and the release MCP transport refusal; do not copy or freeze roster counts. Document in tests that reaching RELEASE_REMOTE_MISSING is authorization evidence, not a completed release. No docs sweep here: parent/full-epic rows retain product-level claims.

ONE FINAL VERIFICATION STEP (DoD 5). Primary complete_task verification command, from repository root, EXACTLY: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec vitest run --root . --config package.json src/release`. Fresh foreground output must name the new authorization test and show nonzero Test Files/Tests counts and exit 0; the positive pairing case cannot be skipped. In this same final step, run each companion leg separately and foreground, retaining exit status/counts: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec vitest run --root . --config package.json src/mcp-tool-allowlist.test.ts src/identity/session-authenticator.test.ts`; `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`; `pnpm typecheck`; `pnpm test`; `pnpm verify:foundation`; `pnpm verify:store`. Honor shared full-suite/browser leases where applicable; never force-release another holder, run full suites concurrently, pipe away a failing status, or count a vacuous filter as green. Compare required repo-wide failures to the merge-base baseline under the path-attribution rail, disclose exact foreign failing paths and lines, and require no new owned-path failures. Root pnpm test excludes apps/** and is not evidence for this daemon change. No schema/runtime command is added, so no digest regeneration or new Control Room gate is implied. Record any permitted foreign baseline red honestly; use the focused release command's fresh successful output as complete_task evidence.

ONE ADVERSARIAL REVIEW / QA HANDOFF, LAST (DoD 1-5). Read the owned diff as an attacker: can an agent or stale/cross-project session masquerade as a durable HUMAN; can a capability omission be hidden by a different earlier refusal; can replay run before authentication; can the unconfigured branch admit more than configured release; can any other kind use the disjunct; did any actor id, roster, evidence rule or release effect change? Perform ONE bounded production mutation removing the ADMIN conjunct, with no peer gate running on those bytes: the HUMAN-with-GOAL-without-ADMIN arm must go RED at its exact authorization assertion, not fail in setup. Restore immediately in finally and prove restoration in a separate call (tracked baseline diff/byte backup, SHA equality for any untracked mutation target); then rerun the primary verification command fresh on restored final bytes so completion evidence is newer than the drill. Confirm listener/store teardown, no secrets in logs, no scratch files left, all three production file caps, and unchanged classification/MCP roster. Cite the exact owner ruling, test count lines, deliberate mutant failure, restore evidence, actual-actor/replay assertions and the unchanged parent dependsOn consumer edge in a row comment under 4500 chars. Report only the five owned paths in complete_step.modifiedFiles; no manual commit/push/merge/rebase. Complete via Moe with the fresh primary command output; QA grades delivered wrapper-attributed bytes, not a dirty-tree-only success. This row certifies authorization, never the parent's still-pending live release journey.

comments.author: governor-9af9af37
comments.content:
🔒 OWNER RULING 18:42Z — **APPROVED: the narrow widening.** @architect-f362f7a6 asked this in the REPL (comment-2ebc58d2) and durably on the row (comment-3b2b9a18) and got no answer; I put it to the owner and they ruled. This comment is the authority. Recorded BEFORE the status change because BLOCKED→PLANNING nulls the block quartet; verbatim block record at the end.

**APPROVED, exactly this and nothing wider:** a currently authenticated, PROJECT-BOUND, durable HUMAN principal holding ADMIN may reach `release.decide`. Actual actor identity is RETAINED — no operator impersonation, no browser credential standing in for the configured operator. MCP exclusion for `release.decide` is UNCHANGED. This is the architect's own proposed option, approved as proposed; the operator step-up alternative was considered and NOT selected, so do not design or implement it.

**THIS IS THE THIRD INSTANCE OF AN ESTABLISHED PATTERN, not a new fence.** I verified both precedents at HEAD in `apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-registry.ts` before taking the question to the owner:
• `approval.decide` — the typed SOFT_POLICY_WAIVER arm at :358, composed BEFORE the operator fence, delegating to `runPolicyWaiverDecideCommand`; a paired browser HUMAN holding ADMIN may decide one while the legacy bytes stay operator-only for that same principal.
• `project.set_agent_provider` — `providerByPairedAdmin` at :375, the one widened kind that ALSO demands ADMIN explicitly, landed today under governor ruling comment-18dc557c for task-136cbab2 (DONE).
Follow the shape those two already set. Prefer reusing the existing composition over minting a new module, a new layer constant, or a new roster entry — the file's own comment at :390-395 says the ADMIN-demanding case "mirrors the SOFT_POLICY_WAIVER POLICY rather than its module shape, so no new code and no new layer constant are minted." Hold to that.

⚠️ **THE TRAP, AND IT IS THE WHOLE REASON THIS NEEDED A RULING. DO NOT REMOVE ANY KIND FROM `OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS`.** `MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS` is DERIVED from it — the registry says so in its own comment at :386-387. Deleting a kind there to "open the write path" opens a SECOND fence in the same edit, silently, and nothing in the diff says so. The narrow instrument is the widening DISJUNCT, composed before the operator fence, exactly as the two precedents do it. An implementation that reaches the goal by shrinking the operator roster is WRONG even if every test passes, and I will treat it as a rejectable defect rather than a style note.

⚠️ **SECOND TRAP, and @architect-f362f7a6 already found it — do not lose it in the plan.** `isDurableHumanPrincipal` (apps/daemon/src/identity/human-approver.ts:22-28) checks ONLY `readPrincipalRecord` FOUND + kind HUMAN. It does NOT prove current authentication, project binding, or ADMIN. All three of those are conditions of THIS approval, so each must be enforced explicitly and separately. A predicate that reads as "durable human" and is treated as "authenticated project-bound admin" would grant strictly more than the owner just approved. Defence in depth is wanted here: redundancy with the ingress capability gate is a feature, per the file's own reasoning.

**WHAT THE APPROVAL DOES NOT COVER:** no other command's authorization changes; no schema, runtime-command, roster or shared-type change is authorized by this ruling; SPEED auto-approval is NOT authority for any of the above — your DoD 1 already says the plan carries an explicit STOP before authority-changing edits, and that clause stands even though the ruling has now arrived, because it is what makes the approval auditable.

**STATUS.** Block premise discharged — moving BLOCKED → PLANNING. @architect-f362f7a6 you may plan and submit now. Your DoD 4 (release.decide stays operator/human-only and MCP-excluded, bidirectional served/excluded roster assertions, plus a non-release operator kind as a negative control) already fences the first trap correctly; keep it exactly as written. Your DoD 3's requirement that a future positive test prove actual authorized browser identity THROUGH THE PRODUCTION INGRESS — rather than relabelling the agent arm or minting an operator-shaped fixture — is right and I am reinforcing it, not relaxing it.

Also on the record: the row's 1-passed focused test proves the configured async entry's non-operator refusal, NOT a real pairing run, and the architect said so plainly rather than overclaiming. Keep that precision in the completion record.
